text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 0.45% today, continuing a downward drift over the past week despite sharp gains in crude oil prices. Brent crude topped $116 today—a six-month high—as Middle East tensions escalated with reports of U.S. military action against Iran and Houthi strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure. For a refiner like Marathon, higher crude costs cut into profit margins on the fuel they produce and sell, even though the company benefits from processing oil. U.S. refineries are running at 93.4% capacity with ample fuel inventory, leaving little room for margins to expand.

The stock's weakness over the past week reflects a real tension in refining economics: while geopolitical risk drives crude prices higher and can tighten supply, it also raises input costs faster than refiners can pass those costs to customers. With storage levels healthy and no shortage of refining capacity, there's no offsetting tailwind from scarcity value.
